Sets up a run for the player: colours the gates, clears the event's zero page, the gate verdicts and the clock, puts the kayak at the start facing up the river, copies the start of the river and its colours to the screen, shows PRESS BUTTON TO START and starts the tune.

Ends the run, when the kayak passes the finish or the clock reaches 9:59: marks every gate not passed as missed, adds the penalties to the time, stores the total in the results table inverted so that a smaller time is a larger score, and draws the results screen.
When one of the hull's sprites touches the banks or a rock, stops the kayak and plays the crash; then adds the push of each touching quarter of the hull to turn the kayak away.
Leftover code that would colour each quarter of the hull touching the bank brown, a debugging aid that nothing calls.
Every third frame would read the water's flow under the kayak from a map at $E000 and push the kayak with it. In this release the map at $E000-$FB57 is all zero, so the push is always nothing.
No current on the frames between.
Counts the three frames between the reads.
Looks for a gate near the kayak; on leaving it judges the crossing: through from the right side and facing the right way scores, anything else is a fault.
Judges the gate just left: a gate skipped is MISSED, the wrong direction FACED WRONG DIRECTION, a second crossing CROSSED MORE THAN ONCE, and the wrong side ENTERED FROM WRONG SIDE.
Notes which side of the gate the kayak is on.
Marks every gate before the one the kayak has reached as missed, one at a time.
Every 18 frames marks the next missed gate.
Records gate Y's verdict X the first time, colours its markers red, adds 20 seconds to the penalty, shows the penalty in the clock sprite and plays the fault sound.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.

Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes.

Clears the gate bit of voice X, ending its note.
